subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless row, even when that blocks plugin workflows that previously patched those rows?
rationale: Ownerless rows cannot be safely attributed to a plugin, but unconditional rejection changes upgrade behavior for existing installations and needs an explicit security-versus-compatibility decision.

options.title: Fail closed after proof
options.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugin runtimes, document the upgrade effect, and require deployed-Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Add explicit migration
options.body: Provide a narrow operator-controlled migration or repair path that assigns ownership only with trustworthy provenance before enforcing the fence.

options.title: Preserve ownerless access
options.body: Allow legacy ownerless patches temporarily with a named deprecation and removal plan, accepting a weaker isolation boundary during the transition.

recommendation.title: Fail closed after proof
recommendation.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugin runtimes, document the upgrade effect, and require deployed-Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to Gateway owner-boundary enforcement and session-store architecture.
